351014.title: The $C^r$ closing lemma for area-preserving diffeomorphisms
351014.literal_statement: Let $M$ be a compact manifold equipped with a symplectic form $\omega$, and let $\operatorname{Diff}^{r}(M,\omega)$ be the space of $C^{r}$ diffeomorphisms preserving $\omega$, where $r=1,2,\ldots,\infty$. A subset is **residual** if it is an intersection of countably many open dense subsets. **The $C^r$ closing lemma.** There exists a residual subset $R\subset\operatorname{Diff}^{r}(M,\omega)$ such that for every $g\in R$, the set $\mathcal{P}(g)$ is dense in $M$. 351026.title: A sharp edge bound in terms of the forcing number

$$

351266.title: Conjecture on Brownian tracking horizon for geometric matchings
351266.literal_statement:
Let $n$ particles move in $d$ dimensions, sampled at intervals of length $\delta$, and let $\widehat{\pi}_k$ be the estimator at time step $k$. Let $T_{\max}$ denote the maximum tracking time before the estimator incurs a macroscopic number of errors. "**Brownian tracking conjecture.**" Suppose that $d\geq2$ and $\delta=n^{-\xi/d}$ for some $\xi\in[2,4]$. Then

$$
T_{\max}\sim\frac{\delta^{1-d/2}}{n}f(n)=n^{\xi/2-\xi/d-1}f(n),
$$

for some $1/\operatorname{polylog}(n)\leq f(n)\leq\operatorname{polylog}(n)$. The heuristic is based on Brownian displacements between snapshots and is explicitly not expected to apply in dimension one, where particle collisions dominate the tracking error; the conjectured behavior remains unproved for the stated higher-dimensional regime.

351524.title: Buhl cycle-condition converse for the weak maximum likelihood threshold
351524.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with at least one edge. An orientation of $G$ is **acyclic** if it has no directed cycles, and a cycle is **stretched** when it has the form $v_1\to v_2\to\dots\to v_k\leftarrow v_1$. Let $\operatorname{wmlt}(G)$ denote the weak maximum likelihood threshold. **Buhl cycle-condition converse.** If $G$ has an acyclic orientation with no stretched cycles, then

$$
\operatorname{wmlt}(G)=2.
$$

The forward implication is known: weak maximum likelihood threshold $2$ implies the existence of such an orientation. The conjecture asserts the converse, completing the rigidity-theoretic characterization of graphs with weak maximum likelihood threshold $2$.

351563.title: Hilton–Zhao's Core Conjecture for class 2 graphs
351563.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a simple connected graph with maximum degree $\Delta\ge 3$. The **core** $G_\Delta$ is the subgraph induced by the vertices of degree $\Delta$, and $\Delta(G_\Delta)\le 2$. Equivalently, every Hilton–Zhao graph $G\ne P^*$ with $\Delta(G)\ge 3$ is overfull. This conjecture would characterize class 2 connected graphs whose core has maximum degree at most $2$, apart from the exceptional graph $P^*$. 351599.title: The Bernstein–Sato formula for the singularity level of local complete intersections
351599.literal_statement:

$$
